description: Code-optimization families for the biomni-code diversity portfolio. Each family lists diagnostic questions and example behavior-preserving interventions. Weights and floors live in intervention_weights.json and are adapted by biomni_code_state.py during a run.

families.name: algorithmic
questions: Is an O(n^2) or worse algorithm used where an exact O(n log n) or O(n) equivalent exists?
Is repeated work inside a loop mathematically invariant and hoistable?
Can early termination or short-circuiting preserve exact outputs?

families.name: vectorization
questions: Are Python/R-level loops doing elementwise numeric work?
Can the operation be expressed with NumPy/SciPy/pandas/data.table kernels without changing dtype, order, or rounding?
Is the reduction order fixed so results stay bitwise-identical?

families.name: data_structures
questions: Is membership testing done on lists instead of sets/dicts?
Are repeated concatenations used where preallocation or a deque/array fits?
Is an object-dtype or boxed representation used where a fixed-width dtype works?

families.name: allocation_memory_layout
questions: Are large temporaries created and discarded inside hot loops?
Are defensive copies made where the source is never mutated?
Can buffers be reused or preallocated without aliasing bugs?

families.name: caching_memoization
questions: Is a pure function recomputed on repeated inputs?
Can parsed metadata, schemas, indexes, or invariant preprocessing be cached?
Is the cache key a content hash so stale caches are detected?

families.name: io_batching
questions: Are files opened/closed repeatedly in loops?
Are small reads/writes batched or buffered?
Is compression/decompression repeated in inner loops?

families.name: serialization
questions: Is data serialized/deserialized repeatedly between stages?
Is a slow text format (CSV/JSON) parsed where a binary format preserves identical values?
Are pickle/JSON encodings doing redundant validation?

families.name: parallelism_concurrency
questions: Is independent work serialized?
Is parallel work coarse enough to amortize scheduling overhead?
Does the parallel reduction order preserve bitwise-identical results?

families.name: compiled_kernels
questions: Is an unavoidable tight loop still in the interpreter?
Can Numba/Cython/pybind11/Rust/Rcpp replace it without changing numerics?
Are compiler flags at the appropriate (behavior-preserving) optimization level?

families.name: startup_imports
questions: Do imports or package loading dominate short CLI runs?
Are heavy dependencies imported at module top level but used rarely?
Is repeated interpreter startup avoidable via batching or a persistent process?

families.name: build_flags
questions: Is compiled code built in debug mode or without -O2/-O3?
Are architecture-specific flags (e.g. -march=native) legal for the deployment target?
Is LTO enabled where it preserves behavior?
